section: Industrial policy - resolutions of 1948, 1956, 1977, 1980 and the New Industrial Policy 1991
subsections: Industries reserved for public sector - numbers across policies

accepted.s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, how many industries were reserved for the public sector in Schedule A?
accepted.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 reserved 17 industries for the public sector under Schedule A.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive policy-wise numerical figure and eliminate nearby values.
accepted.sec: Industries reserved for public sector - numbers across policies

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the industries reserved for the public sector:
1. Eight industries were reserved under the New Industrial Policy, 1991.
2. The number was subsequently reduced to three.
3. After May 2001, only atomic energy and railway operations remained reserved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The number declined from eight in 1991 to three and ultimately to two after defence was opened to private participation in May 2001.
accepted.tq: Track the policy sequence from the initial number to the present position.
accepted.sec: Industries reserved for public sector - numbers across policies

accepted.s: Which one of the following was opened to the private sector in May 2001, thereby reducing the industries reserved for the public sector?
accepted.x: Defence production, including arms and ammunition, was opened to the private sector in May 2001. Atomic energy and railway operations continued in the reserved category.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the industry removed from the reserved list from those retained.
accepted.sec: Industries reserved for public sector - numbers across policies

accepted.s: Which of the following policy resolutions is associated with the expression ‘Economic Constitution of India’ and ‘Bible of State Capitalism’?
accepted.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 is described as the Economic Constitution of India and the Bible of State Capitalism.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive descriptive label with the correct policy resolution.
accepted.sec: Policy resolution → label or link  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Industrial Policy Resolution, 1980 — District Industries Centres
Industrial Policy Statement, 1973 — Joint sector concept
Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 — District Industries Centres
accepted.x: The Industrial Policy Statement, 1973 is associated with the joint sector concept and the core sector list. District Industries Centres were associated with the 1977 policy, while economic federalism was linked with the 1980 policy.
accepted.tq: Use policy-label association and reject swapped years.
accepted.sec: Policy resolution → label or link  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The beginning of the ‘licence-permit-quota raj’ in India is generally associated with which policy resolution?
accepted.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 is associated with the beginning of the licence-permit-quota raj.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy linked with the historical label rather than the later reform policy.
accepted.sec: Policy resolution → label or link  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the principal purpose of the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969?
o: To control private monopolies and concentration of economic power
To promote foreign direct investment in high-priority industries
To provide automatic approval for technology agreements
accepted.x: The MRTP Act, 1969 aimed to control private monopolies and prevent concentration of economic power. Its enactment followed the recommendations associated with the Dutt Committee.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the objective of the MRTP Act from objectives of later liberalisation measures.
accepted.sec: MRTP Act 1969 - purpose and replacement  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the MRTP framework:
1. The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969 and came into force in 1970.
2. The asset threshold for MRTP firms was raised to Rs. 100 crore in 1985.
3. The market-share criterion was reduced from 33 per cent to 25 per cent in 1984.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Act was enacted in 1969 and brought into force in 1970; the market-share limit was reduced in 1984 and the asset limit was raised in 1985.
accepted.tq: Check each date and numerical change independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: MRTP Act 1969 - purpose and replacement  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was replaced by which legislation?
accepted.x: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the MRTP Act. The MRTP Commission was replaced by the Competition Commission of India.
accepted.tq: Use the enactment-year trap to distinguish the Competition Act from FEMA.
accepted.sec: MRTP Act 1969 - purpose and replacement  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What was the effect of the New Industrial Policy, 1991 on the MRTP asset threshold of Rs. 100 crore?
o: It made the threshold applicable only to public sector firms
It reduced the threshold to Rs. 50 crore
It doubled the threshold to Rs. 200 crore
It scrapped the threshold for large firms
accepted.x: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 scrapped the MRTP asset threshold. Large firms no longer required prior approval for expansion, mergers or takeovers merely because of their asset size.
accepted.tq: Apply the reform measure to the specific regulatory restriction being removed.
accepted.sec: MRTP Act 1969 - purpose and replacement  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order:
A. Sick Industrial Companies Act
B. MRTP Act
C. Industries (Development and Regulation) Act
D. FERA
accepted.x: The correct order is Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951; MRTP Act, 1969; FERA, 1973; and Sick Industrial Companies Act, 1985.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest enactments, then place the middle years.
accepted.sec: Chronology of regulatory enactments  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Sick Industrial Companies Act was enacted in 1985, not 1984. The other three year-pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the single altered year in an otherwise familiar chronology.
accepted.sec: Chronology of regulatory enactments  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The R. K. Hazari report of 1967 primarily examined which subject?
accepted.x: The R. K. Hazari report examined industrial licensing and reported that big business houses had cornered licences.
accepted.tq: Match the committee or report with its precise policy subject.
accepted.sec: Licensing committees → chairman  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who chaired the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee which submitted its report in 1969?
accepted.x: The Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee was chaired by Subimal Dutt. Its report was submitted in 1969 and contributed to the enactment of the MRTP Act.
accepted.tq: Separate the report author from the later legislation and its commonly used committee name.
accepted.sec: Licensing committees → chairman  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Item reservation for small-scale industries in India began in which year?
accepted.x: Item reservation for small-scale industries began in 1967. It continued after 1991, while the last reserved items were dereserved in 2015.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the origin year from later policy changes affecting SSI reservation.
accepted.sec: Reservation for small-scale industries - origin and dereservation  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding small-scale industries is correct?
o: The last SSI items were dereserved in 1980.
The 1977 policy defined tiny units and the 1980 policy raised SSI investment limits.
SSI item reservation began only after the New Industrial Policy, 1991.
The 1977 policy abolished tiny units and the 1980 policy ended SSI reservation.
accepted.x: The 1977 policy introduced the definition of tiny units, while the 1980 policy raised investment limits for small-scale industries. SSI item reservation began in 1967 and the last items were dereserved in 2015.
accepted.tq: Keep the two closely related policy changes in their correct year-policy combination.
accepted.sec: Reservation for small-scale industries - origin and dereservation  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The New Industrial Policy was announced on which date?
accepted.x: The New Industrial Policy was announced on 24 July 1991.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the exact day-month-year and nearby reform dates.
accepted.sec: Foreign investment and technology agreements - automatic approval, 51% limit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Automatic approval up to 51 per cent foreign equity under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 initially applied to which category?
o: High-priority, high-investment and high-technology industries on the specified list
accepted.x: Automatic approval up to 51 per cent foreign equity applied to a specified list of high-priority, high-investment and high-technology industries. It was not available to all industries without restriction.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘all’ and identify the specified sectoral category.
accepted.sec: Foreign investment and technology agreements - automatic approval, 51% limit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was permitted under the foreign investment and technology provisions of the New Industrial Policy, 1991?
1. Automatic approval for foreign technology agreements in high-priority industries
2. Use of foreign brand names and trademarks
3. Establishment of the Foreign Investment Promotion Board to speed approvals
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three measures formed part of the liberalised foreign investment and technology framework associated with the 1991 policy.
accepted.tq: Test several related liberalisation measures together and use the complete combination only when all are supported.
accepted.sec: Foreign investment and technology agreements - automatic approval, 51% limit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the later foreign investment approval framework is correct?
o: FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and approvals are processed through the FIF portal.
FIPB continues to be the sole approval authority for all foreign investment.
The negative-list approach was replaced by a complete prohibition on foreign equity.
accepted.x: The Foreign Investment Promotion Board was abolished in June 2017, and approvals were shifted to the FIF portal. FDI up to 100 per cent under the automatic route is permitted in most sectors subject to the applicable negative list.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional change while rejecting absolute statements about FDI.
accepted.sec: Foreign investment and technology agreements - automatic approval, 51% limit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The FIF portal was integrated with the National Single Window System in which month and year?
accepted.x: The FIF portal was integrated with the National Single Window System in August 2022.
accepted.tq: Retain the precise month-year associated with the administrative reform.
accepted.sec: Foreign investment and technology agreements - automatic approval, 51% limit  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: How many industries were subject to compulsory industrial licensing in July 1991?
accepted.x: In July 1991, 18 industries were under compulsory industrial licensing.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the initial licensing count from the later reduced counts.
accepted.sec: Licensing - industries under compulsory licensing, then and now  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which group of industries was delicensed in 1993?
o: Electronic aerospace equipment, defence equipment and drugs
accepted.x: Automobiles, white goods and leather were delicensed in 1993.
accepted.tq: Match the year of delicensing with the correct group rather than a later residual category.
accepted.sec: Licensing - industries under compulsory licensing, then and now  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the reduction of compulsory licensing:
1. Electronic goods were delicensed in December 1996.
2. Five more industries were delicensed in July 1997.
3. Coal and petroleum were delicensed under the Budget for 1998–99.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. These successive measures reduced the number of industries under compulsory licensing to six by the 1998–99 Budget stage.
accepted.tq: Follow the dated stages of deregulation in sequence.
accepted.sec: Licensing - industries under compulsory licensing, then and now  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the five industries presently identified as remaining under compulsory licensing?
accepted.x: Drugs and pharmaceuticals were later delicensed. The remaining categories include alcohol, tobacco, hazardous chemicals, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, and industrial explosives.
accepted.tq: Find the item removed from the older six-item list to obtain the current five.
accepted.sec: Licensing - industries under compulsory licensing, then and now  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
